items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: like Hitler did, that kind of mentality

ctx.x: So what does he do? He goes and gets a job with one of these daily papers in Boston and he never wrote another word about jazz -- making a lot of money writing about other stuff. Unfortunately, he died writing for this paper in Boston.*

But those people used jazz, and those are the parasites, and that's a cynical way to break into the field, by criticizing a big name singer and saying she stinks. But that is cynical, like the Ayatollah, he doesn't care whose head rolls, or like Hitler did, that kind of mentality. So many in the jazz world are not sincere, associated with the jazz movement. They don't respect jazz musicians. A lot of these guys come around simpering and smiling, with their little pencils and papers, people with the magazines, and…

Like Atlantic Records, the Ertegun brothers, they were staunch supporters, their father was the Ambassador to Turkey years ago, and once they got a taste of American Ambassador from Turkey to the U.S.
